user_query: My landlord in Bengaluru is refusing to return my security deposit of Rs 1,50,000 after I vacated the flat on 1 month notice. What are my legal rights and options?
expected_statutory_basis: Model Tenancy Act / State Rent Control Laws
key_legal_principles: Landlord can only deduct reasonable, pre-agreed wear-and-tear or unpaid utility bills/rent.
Under Model Tenancy principles, residential security deposit is capped at a maximum of two months' rent.
First step: Issue a formal legal notice demanding refund within 15 days.
If unpaid: File a summary civil suit for recovery of money (Order 37 CPC) or approach Rent Court/Authority.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Inform user that security deposit recovery is governed by the registered rental agreement and local state tenancy act.

user_query: Can my landlord suddenly cut off my water and electricity connection because I delayed rent by 10 days?
expected_sections: Delhi Rent Control Act Sec 45 / Karnataka Rent Act Sec 38
key_legal_principles: No landlord has the legal right to disconnect essential supplies or services (water, electricity, sanitary services) to coerce a tenant.
Withholding essential supplies is a punishable offence and an illegal act under state rent laws.
Tenant can immediately petition the Rent Authority/Controller for urgent restoration of services and compensation.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Emergency step: Contact local police station if essential utilities are physically vandalized or locked.

user_query: My landlord gave me a verbal notice to vacate the house in 2 days. Is this valid under Indian law?
key_legal_principles: Verbal notice is legally invalid for determining a lease.

Under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, a notice to quit must be in writing, signed, and delivered with at least 15 days notice expiring with the end of a month of tenancy (for residential leases).
A landlord cannot forcibly dispossess a tenant without due process of law.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Clarify that forcible extra-judicial eviction can be resisted through an injunction from a civil court.

user_query: I bought a laptop for Rs 65,000 from an online marketplace. The screen was broken on delivery, but customer support refused refund or replacement. Where can I file a complaint?
key_legal_principles: Selling damaged goods and refusing refund/replacement constitutes 'deficiency in service' and 'unfair trade practice'.
The consumer can file a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
Complaints can be filed online via the e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) or National Consumer Helpline (1915).
District Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction up to Rs 50 Lakhs (and complainant can file where they reside).
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Preserve unboxing video, courier slip, invoice, and email correspondence as evidence.

user_query: What is the pecuniary jurisdiction limit of District, State, and National Consumer Commissions?
key_legal_principles: District Commission: Claims where value of goods/services paid as consideration does not exceed Rs 50 Lakhs.
State Commission: Claims where value exceeds Rs 50 Lakhs but does not exceed Rs 2 Crores.
National Commission (NCDRC): Claims where value exceeds Rs 2 Crores.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Jurisdiction is calculated based on consideration actually paid, not on total compensation claimed.

user_query: What is the limitation period for filing a complaint in the Consumer Forum?
key_legal_principles: The limitation period is 2 years from the date on which the cause of action arose.
A complaint may be entertained after 2 years only if the complainant satisfies the Commission that they had sufficient cause for delay.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Never miss the 2-year deadline as condonation of delay is at the Commission's discretion.

user_query: A client gave me a cheque of Rs 3,00,000 which bounced due to 'Insufficient Funds'. What are the strict legal steps and deadlines to file a case under Section 138?
key_legal_principles: Cheque must have been presented within validity period (3 months).
Bank return memo received: Statutory demand notice must be dispatched within 30 days of receiving return memo.
Notice must give 15 days to the drawer to make payment from date of receipt.
If drawer fails to pay within 15 days, cause of action arises; criminal complaint must be filed within 30 days before Judicial Magistrate (Sec 142).
Interim compensation up to 20% of cheque amount can be ordered under Section 143A.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Strict adherence to 30-day notice and 30-day filing limitation is jurisdictional; any delay must be condoned by court.

user_query: Can a person be imprisoned for a cheque bounce case under Section 138?
key_legal_principles: Yes, Section 138 is a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
The offence is bailable and compoundable under Section 147 of the Act.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: It is compoundable at any stage, even during trial or appeal upon payment.

user_query: What are my rights if a police officer stops and arrests me without a warrant in India?
key_legal_principles: Right to know grounds of arrest immediately and whether offence is bailable.
Right to have a relative or nominated friend informed immediately of the arrest and place of custody.
Right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice.
Mandatory medical examination at time of arrest (Sec 54 / BNSS Sec 53).
Mandatory production before the nearest Judicial Magistrate within 24 hours (excluding journey time).
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: D.K. Basu guidelines laid down by Supreme Court must be followed by every arresting officer.

user_query: A local police station refused to lodge my FIR for an assault that happened in an adjacent district. What is a Zero FIR and what can I do?
expected_statutory_basis: Supreme Court guidelines (Lalita Kumari v. Govt of UP)
key_legal_principles: A police station cannot refuse to register an FIR for a cognizable offence citing territorial jurisdiction.
They must register a 'Zero FIR', initiate urgent action/medical aid, and subsequently transfer the docket to the jurisdictional station.

If police still refuse: Send complaint in writing to Superintendent of Police (SP/DCP) by registered post under BNSS 173(4) / CrPC 154(3), or file private complaint before Magistrate under BNSS 223 / CrPC 156(3).
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Zero FIR is now statutorily codified under Section 173 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

user_query: What is the difference between Anticipatory Bail and Regular Bail under the new criminal codes?
key_legal_principles: Anticipatory Bail (BNSS 482 / CrPC 438): Sought prior to arrest when a person has reasonable apprehension of being arrested in a non-bailable offence. Operates at the moment of arrest.
Regular Bail (BNSS 480/483 / CrPC 437/439): Sought after the person has already been arrested and is in police or judicial custody.
Jurisdiction for anticipatory bail lies with the Sessions Court or High Court.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Anticipatory bail cannot be claimed as a matter of absolute right and is subject to judicial discretion based on nature and gravity of accusation.

user_query: I filed an RTI application with the municipal corporation regarding road maintenance funds, but received no response after 35 days. What is my remedy?
key_legal_principles: Public Information Officer (PIO) must provide information within 30 days of receipt of application.
Failure to respond within 30 days is deemed refusal under Section 7(2).
Remedy: File a First Appeal under Section 19(1) before the designated First Appellate Authority (FAA) within 30 days.
If First Appeal is rejected or unresponded within 30-45 days, file a Second Appeal before the State/Central Information Commission under Section 19(3).
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: PIO is liable for penalty of Rs 250 per day up to Rs 25,000 under Section 20 for unjustified delay.

user_query: Who is eligible for free legal aid in India and where should an indigent person apply?
key_legal_principles: Eligible categories under Section 12: Women and children, members of SC/ST, victims of trafficking/begar, persons with disability, victims of mass disaster/violence, industrial workmen, persons in custody.
Income criteria: Persons whose annual income is less than prescribed state limit (typically Rs 3,00,000 in Delhi/many states; Rs 5,00,000 for SC/High Court in certain states).
Where to apply: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at district court, Taluk Legal Services Committee, or State Legal Services Authority (SLSA).
National Legal Aid Helpline: 15100 (toll-free).
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Free legal aid covers lawyer fees, court fees, drafting charges, and process fees completely free of cost.

user_query: The builder promised possession of my flat by December 2022, but the building is still under construction in 2026. What can I claim under RERA?
key_legal_principles: Under Section 18(1), allottee has two distinct choices:
Option A (Withdraw from project): Builder must refund full amount received with prescribed interest (SBI MCLR + 2%) and compensation.
Option B (Stay in project): Builder must pay monthly interest for every month of delay till possession is handed over.
Complaint can be filed under Section 31 before the State Real Estate Regulatory Authority.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Check RERA registration number and official RERA project completion date on state RERA portal.

user_query: What is the procedure and timeline to claim compensation for a road accident injury in India?
key_legal_principles: Claim petition must be filed before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT).
Under the 2019 amendment (Section 166(3)), a claim petition must be filed within 6 months of the occurrence of the accident.
Police must prepare and submit Detailed Accident Report (DAR) within statutory time frame.
Victim or legal heirs can claim against driver, owner, and insurance company.
mandatory_escalation_or_disclaimer: Strict 6-month limitation introduced by 2019 amendment must be guarded against.
